newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen weak as foreigners sideline.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen weak as foreigners sideline.

text.p: Thai stocks were seen moving lower on Wednesday as foreign investors will likely stay on the sidelines after Thailand's move to cut off access of baht funding through the stock market, brokers said.

"Over the past few days, trading was dominated by foreigners selling stocks to raise their much-needed baht," said a broker at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities. "The central bank's stricter measures make it difficult to do so."
The SET index on Tuesday closed down 7.24 points at 527.22 on foreign selling after the Bank of Thailand's measures.
The central bank asked bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks among foreigners in a measure to curb efforts by speculators to raise baht funds through short sales.
The central bank also required non-resident investors selling Thai stocks to remit their funds in foreign currencies only.

The bank said the temporary moves are aimed at curbing baht supply available to currency speculators who attacked on baht last month and are desperate to raise baht funds to cover short baht/dollar positions.
